## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Aṭṭhipuñja Sutta* ("A Heap of Bones", Iti 24) is a short discourse located in the first division of the *Itivuttaka* (PTS It 17) [SuttaCentral]. The teaching underscores the immense scope of transmigration (*saṁsāra*) by stating that over the course of wandering in rebirth, a single individual would accumulate a heap of bones as large as a mountain, assuming the bones were preserved and assembled together [SuttaCentral]. The text is also cited in early paracanonical and exegetical works, including the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 1.1) and the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37) [SuttaCentral].

The discourse exhibits extensive canonical and cross-tradition parallels. SuttaCentral identifies an exact Pali parallel in the *Puggalasutta* of the *Anamatagga Saṁyutta* (SN 15.10), as well as Chinese Āgama counterparts in the *Saṁyuktāgama* (SA 947, SA2 340, SA3 11), the *Ekottarika Āgama* (EA2 30), and T 765.3 [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus agree on the close alignment with the *Anamatagga Saṁyutta*, with DharmaNexus recording nearly verbatim reuse (§2.3–6.4 ↔ SN 15.10, similarity 0.99) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records substantial Pali-internal text reuse with the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (§3.1–4.4) and the *Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā*, alongside formulaic shared material with other *Itivuttaka* discourses such as Iti 14 and Iti 26 [DharmaNexus]. At the verse level, SuttaCentral notes parallels in the *Dhammapada* (Dhp 191), the Sanskrit *Divyāvadāna*, the *Udānavarga* (UV 27), the *Theragāthā* (Thag 21.1), and several poems in the *Therīgāthā* (Thig 7.2, 7.3, 13.3, 13.4) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus additionally aligns the text with Chinese translations of the *Madhyama Āgama* and *Saṁyuktāgama*, as well as the Tibetan translation of the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
